title: Blocked-residency orchestrator for token-affinity GPU eviction and throttling
creator: Ava Jensen
description:
Goal: implement a blocked-residency orchestrator for the KV cache that reduces OOMs and tail latency when GPUs are oversubscribed while preserving high batching efficiency. This ticket scopes the design, prototype, and validation plan for a block-oriented residency map that assigns token-affinity scores and coordinates eviction waves and host spill with minimal interference to the batch scheduling hot path.

Background: Continuous batching benefits from long-lived KV fragments staying resident on GPU. Oversubscription and large variable-length sequences cause fragmentation and non-deterministic page swaps, which increase latency and drop throughput. Current heuristics evict on LRU boundaries at coarse granularity and can evict active KV slices used by in-flight batches. We need a more block-aware, token-affinity-driven residency controller that cooperates with the scheduler and batching layer.

Design summary:
- Data structures: a striped residency map (resident_map) composed of fixed-size blocks (4–16MiB tunable) aligned to GPU page boundaries. Each block holds metadata as a compact 64-bit token-affinity signature, reference count, last_access_epoch, and a residency-state enum (resident, staged, spilled, pinned).
- Token-affinity scoring: compute an affinity fingerprint per request based on recent token IDs and request priority. Affinity is used to score blocks on access; hot blocks get a soft-residency boost to avoid being chosen for eviction within the next N scheduling epochs.
- Block cohorts and eviction wavefront: blocks are grouped into cohorts by LRU epoch buckets. Eviction picks entire cohorts when possible to reduce fragmentation; within a cohort we prefer low-affinity blocks, then staged blocks, then resident blocks with refcount==0. When cohorts are tight, we trigger an eviction wavefront that migrates blocks to a host-side spill ring buffer in batch units aligned to block boundaries.
- Host spill and pipelined restore: spilled blocks are written to a host ring buffer (append-only) and compressed with a low-latency codec. Restoration is pipelined and prioritized by affinity; high-affinity blocks are prefetched before known batch windows.
- Scheduler integration: the residency orchestrator exposes a non-blocking check_residency(block_set) API returning residency decisions and an optional prefetch hint. The continuous batcher consults residency checks before sealing a batch; if the orchestrator signals potential miss rates above a threshold, the batcher can split or apply fast-path routing to a compatible model variant pinned to host memory.
- Backpressure and soft-SLOs: when available resident memory dips below soft-residency thresholds, the orchestrator sets per-tenant backpressure flags (graceful throttling) and emits metrics for the autoscaler to request extra capacity or capacity swap.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered:
- Per-token granularity would be ideal for precision but is too expensive in metadata overhead and would complicate coalescing. Blocked approach balances metadata size vs. eviction precision.
- Eager pinning of blocks for in-flight batches reduces misses but increases fragmentation; we implement ephemeral pin windows that auto-release after epoch ticks.
- Using host SSD spill vs. host RAM ring: SSD spill has higher capacity but higher restore latency; ring-buffer in host RAM chosen for fast P99 restore at the cost of stricter host memory budgeting.

Observability and metrics:
- resid_blocks_total, resid_blocks_resident, resid_blocks_spilled, resid_block_affinity_hot_pct, spill_write_bytes/sec, spill_restore_ms_p50/p95/p99, eviction_cohort_size_avg, batch_miss_rate_by_model, batch_miss_rate_by_seq_len_bucket.
- Trace fields: block_id, cohort_id, affinity_score, decision_reason (prefetch/evict/retain), caller_batch_id. These should be emitted to the trace pipeline for sampling.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Prototype integrated with the runtime's batcher and KV allocator demonstrating reduction in P99 latency on a mixed-length workload under 1.8x GPU oversubscription compared to baseline.
2) No increase in median latency > 5% on steady-state workloads.
3) Unit tests for residency map operations and stress tests for eviction wavefront correctness.
4) Dashboards showing the new metrics and an automated canary for rollback on degraded tail latency.

Rollout plan: canary on non-critical tenants for 48 hours, compare batch_miss_rate and P99 latency, then broaden to k8s pool subset, then full cluster. Rollback if P99 increases > 10% or error rate spikes.

Related notes: this design must avoid adding synchronous GPU-to-host transfers on the fast path; all restores should be asynchronous with completion callbacks handled by the batcher integration layer.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ava Jensen: Created ticket after spike showing tail latency spikes during weekend stress test. Initial design draft attached.
2025-02-13 - Ravi Patel: First-pass implementation of resident_map prototype in branch feat/block-residency. Placeholder block size set to 8MiB; need benchmark matrix for 4/8/16MiB.
2025-02-14 - Maria Gomez (PM): Prioritize correctness over max packing. Add test plans for multi-tenant fairness and tenant-level backpressure metrics.
2025-02-15 - QA: Discovered race where pinned blocks were not released on request abort; added ephemeral pin window instrumentation. Patch landed in PR #4872.
2025-02-16 - Engineering review (K. Huang): Suggested moving coil-and-wave eviction into a background worker to avoid fast-path contention. Agreed; refactor scheduled.
2025-02-18 - Performance team: Initial microbenchmarks show 22% P99 improvement with 8MiB blocks on mixture-2 workload at 1.5x oversubscription. Need full cluster test before canary.
Next actions: finalize host ring buffer sizing calc, add compression codec hook, run cluster-scale integration test, schedule canary for 2025-03-03 if results pass.
